news.title: Mike Penders: My Football Firsts
news.body_en: We hear from Mike Penders, fresh from making his Premier League debut for Chelsea, about his earliest experiences of the game. The goalkeeper, who came on in our 2-0 win at Everton last weekend, answers our quickfire questions so Blues fans can get to know him better… What was the first football match you went to? That would be the Belgium national team in the King Baudouin Stadium when I was kid. What was the first football kit you owned? It was a Belgium shirt, the outfield one not the goalkeeper one! What was the first team you played for? Boorsem Sport, a local team where I live. They’re maybe not the first, but I would say goalkeeper coaches from Genk from the past: Paul Peeters, Gilbert Roex and Koen Witters. Who was your first team-mate who became a friend? That is my best friend, he is called Gerben. We played together when we were about eight years old. Who was your first professional game against? It was in the second division in Belgium. They were professional by then. It was for Genk’s second team against Waasland-Beveren. Who was your first goal against? I remember scoring once when I was very young! It was on the very small pitches and I was playing for Boorsem. It will stay in my mind forever! Can you remember the first time somebody recognised you in public? That was when I was at Genk, when I started to play some games there. I can remember it a little bit. What was your first emotion when you signed for Chelsea? It was amazing, of course. One of the biggest teams in the world. You don’t need a lot of persuasion to do that!

news.title: Chelsea Women's Constant Contact September Goal of the Month revealed!
news.body_en: Wieke Kaptein's sublime strike against Austria Vienna in the UEFA Women's Champions League has been voted as our Constant Contact Goal of the Month for September! The Dutch midfielder broke the deadlock in our opening Champions League league-phase fixture, picking up a loose ball 30 yards from goal before taking two touches to beat a defender and thundering an effort off the underside of the crossbar. Kaptein hit the ball sweetly beyond the powerless goalkeeper to give us a memorable winner. Our No. 19 has played a big role in our unbeaten start to the campaign, featuring in all nine games so far this season and starting in eight of those encounters. Her strike was the clear winner among Blues fans, receiving 41 per cent of all votes cast. Alyssa Thompson's winner against Arsenal finished second with 14 per cent, while Lauren James' fine strike against Aston Villa and Lexi Potter's effort against Birmingham both received 10 per cent to share third place.

news.title: OTD: Jimmy Floyd thumps in four!
news.body_en: Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink had already endeared himself to Blues supporters when he hit new heights a couple of months into his Chelsea career, smashing four goals in against Coventry City at Stamford Bridge 26 years ago today. Jimmy joined from Atletico Madrid in the summer of 2000 and opened his account for the Blues in the 2-0 Community Shield win over Manchester United at Wembley. He then bagged on his Premier League debut for us, too, with his next three goals coming against Arsenal, Manchester United and Liverpool. Coventry arrived at the Bridge on Saturday 21 October 2000 fresh from beating Tottenham, but they were blown away by a superb Chelsea display that showcased what our side, with newly-appointed Claudio Ranieri at the helm, was capable of. Hasselbaink won and then converted a penalty in the 25th minute to get the rout underway, and he doubled our lead shortly before the break with a bending effort having cut in from the left flank. It was a goal we would see many times again! After Gianfranco Zola had made it 3-0, Hasselbaink completed his hat-trick with a tap-in - although one of the more emphatic variety, of course! - and then bagged his fourth with another pinpoint finish. His quartet of goals were scored in just 33 minutes. Sub Tore-Andre Flo added a sixth with what would prove his final Chelsea goal before departing for Rangers, with Ed de Goey's clean sheet spoiled by Cedric Roussel in the 89th minute. Still, there was no doubt who the day belonged to. Hasselbaink finished as the Premier League's top goalscorer with 23 goals, and there was no more profitable day than his one against Coventry at the Bridge.

news.title: Training gallery: The Blues return to work
Lexi Potter on a whirlwind few weeks for club and country
news.body_en: The rise of Lexi Potter from Chelsea Academy graduate to regularly featuring for Sonia Bompastor’s team and earning her first senior England cap may come as a surprise to some, but those who have followed her career closely will have understood she was destined for the top. Breaking records from an early age, Potter became the youngest player in women’s football history to sign a professional contract when she penned her first deal at Chelsea in 2023 at the age of 17. After two successful campaigns on loan with Crystal Palace, the midfielder earned her first Blues appearance at the start of last season when she came on as a 72nd-minute substitute in our 4-0 win against Paris FC in October. By March, she had played her way to a first-team start, which came at home against Brighton & Hove Albion. Bompastor’s faith was rewarded with a goal from Potter in a 2-1 win over the Seagulls. It was a sign of what was to come. After ten games in all competitions this season, the 20-year-old has featured nine times, scoring once. In the Women’s Super League, she has played 376 minutes - only seven of our players have spent more time on the pitch than Potter. Of course then, it was no wonder that she was on England head coach Sarina Wiegman’s radar when it was time to make her selections for the October internationals. And sure enough, she became England Women’s legacy number 244 when she was named on the teamsheet against Greece in Leicester. Shy and humble, Potter says she’s not yet processed making her senior England debut. But if her form is anything to go by, the spotlight on her is not going away anytime soon. ‘No, not yet,’ she says when asked if the night at the King Power Stadium has sunk in. ‘It's been a quick turnaround from the international break to coming back at Chelsea, but it's been a really good few weeks, and definitely a time I'll never forget. 244 🦁 ❤️Lexi Potter is set to make her #Lionesses debut tonight! 👊 pic.twitter.com/CTrtTOyMxu ‘It was really special. It's something that you always work towards as a young girl, and I'm very grateful and very proud to have done that.’ If anything were to highlight how Potter has remained grounded, it’s how she describes getting the call from Wiegman. ‘I was just at home, in my room, and I wasn't expecting it at all,’ she explains. ‘So when I got the call, I was really happy and very excited.’ Chelsea supporters have seen Potter’s relationship with Keira Walsh blossom on and off the field at club level. That meant the youngster had a ready-made mentor when she joined the senior England camp earlier this month. ‘There aren't many players better in the number six role than Keira to learn from, and I'm very lucky to get the opportunity to be playing alongside her at the moment,’ Potter continued. ‘There are a lot of things in her game that I can learn from and hopefully add to mine, but as the minutes go by, hopefully the partnership will just continue to get stronger. Hopefully we can go very far.’ On current evidence, it appears that the partnership will continue to go far, as Potter suggests. For both club and country.

news.title: Danny Welbeck on leadership, family and honouring our communities
news.body_en: As part of Black History Month, Chelsea FC and Football Black List brought together Danny Welbeck and Football Black List co-founder Leon Mann for a conversation on leadership, family and community. It reflects Chelsea’s ‘Beyond Blue’ approach: building a more inclusive culture, increasing representation and tackling bias in any form. Danny highlights the importance of giving everyone a voice and creating a safe environment. The conversation also ties into this year’s theme, 'Honouring Our Communities'. Danny reflects on how his family shaped his career, his values and his approach to leadership. He and Leon discuss what leadership means in football today, the value of positive role models, and the responsibility experienced players have to support and create opportunities for the next generation. Football Black List celebrates the achievements of Black professionals across football, with African and Caribbean heritage at its heart. Co-founded by Leon Mann and Rodney Hinds, it champions Black excellence, increases visibility and representation, and backs the next generation of leaders in the game. news.title: Mike Penders breaks 21-year Chelsea record after Premier League debut
news.body_en: Mike Penders became Chelsea’s youngest goalkeeper in Premier League history when he replaced Emiliano Martinez in the second half of Saturday’s victory at Everton. The Belgian came on to make his English top-flight debut at the age of 21 years and 78 days, surpassing Lenny Pidgeley as our youngest keeper in the league since 1992. While Penders now holds the Premier League record for the Blues, our all-time youngest goalkeeper remains Kingsley Whiffen. Whiffen was just 16 years and 157 days old when he made his solitary appearance away to Leicester City in Division One in 1967. Whiffen is followed by Steve Francis (17 years, 130 days) and Les Fridge (17 years, 251 days) as our youngest keepers. Here is a closer look at the five youngest goalkeepers to feature for Chelsea in the Premier League era after Penders broke the record, which had stood for over 20 years… Penders was called into action as a second-half substitute at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday, replacing the injured Martinez. The young Belgian, who spent last season on loan at Strasbourg, showed great composure under pressure. One dominant punch on the edge of the box caught the eye as he helped us see out a first league clean sheet since January. Charlton Athletic (h) – 7 May 2005 Academy graduate Pidgeley previously held the Premier League record. Pidgeley was our third-choice keeper, behind the great Petr Cech and Carlo Cudicini, in the title-winning seasons of 2004/05 and 2005/06. He made his Blues bow on the day we lifted the Premier League trophy for the first time, brought on by Jose Mourinho late into our eventual 1-0 success over Charlton. He played one more game the following season before moving on to Millwall. Manchester United (h) – 15 August 2004 Petr Cech was not long 22 when he made his Chelsea debut on the opening day of that incredible 2004/05 season. He kept a clean sheet against Manchester United at Stamford Bridge, setting the tone for a record-breaking campaign and career. Cech has kept the most clean sheets in Premier League history, and at Chelsea went on to win four Premier League titles, four FA Cups and, of course, the Champions League. After three successful years on loan at Atletico Madrid, Thibaut Courtois returned to Stamford Bridge to make his Premier League debut on the opening weekend of the 2014/15 season. The towering Belgian displaced Cech between the posts that year, helping the Blues claim the Premier League title. Southampton (a) – 4 December 2024 Rounding off the top five is Filip Jorgensen. Having signed from Villarreal in the summer of 2024, Jorgensen made his first Premier League appearance during a big midweek victory against Southampton. news.title: PGA Division 1 report: Chelsea Women Under-18s 5-1 Tottenham Hotspur
news.body_en: Chelsea Women Under-18s, who play in the PGA Under-21 Women's League, began our Women’s PGA National League Division 1 campaign with a 5-1 victory over Tottenham Hotspur at Cobham, with Manaka Matsukubo scoring a hat-trick. Spurs took the lead with just 15 seconds on the clock, but Matsukubo levelled on eight minutes and Lola Brown struck twice before half-time to put the Blues in control. Matsukubo added two more after the break, completing her hat-trick with a superb volley on 70 minutes. First-team players Brown, Nelly Las, Chloe Sarwie and Matsukubo were all involved for Leanne Champ’s side. It was Brown’s third appearance for the Under-18s, while Las, Sarwie and Matsukubo each made their second appearance for the team this season. Spurs went ahead straight from kick-off. A long ball forward was not cleared by the Chelsea defence and midfield, and Nife Aramide collected on the edge of the area before finding the bottom corner. The early lead did not last long. Matsukubo was unable to convert at the end of a Rebekah Pierce cross, but Keira Johnson (pictured top) quickly won the ball back on the edge of the area and slid it through for Matsukubo, who calmly placed her finish past the onrushing Sophie Jackson. A rapid counter-attack put Chelsea ahead before the half-hour mark. Matsukubo cleared the ball from our own box and Chelsea N’Drin recovered it, allowing Brown to drive forward into the Spurs half. A well-timed one-two with Matsukubo took Brown into the box, where she cut onto her left foot and finished at the near post. Brown added a third as half-time approached. She pressed a Spurs goal-kick aggressively, intercepted a pass from the goalkeeper and quickly passed into a virtually empty net. Champ made three changes at the break, with Elise Christian, Stevie Sinclair and Jahmya Putman replacing Gabi Storey, Johnson and N’Drin. Sophie Leach came on for Sarwie on 61 minutes. The Blues scored a fourth on 63 minutes. Matsukubo found Pierce out wide on the left, and as Pierce drove inside she laid the ball off to Matsukubo on the overlap. Matsukubo jinked past three Spurs defenders in the box and bent her shot into the far corner. She saved the best for last seven minutes later. A headed clearance from a Chelsea corner fell to Matsukubo on the edge of the box, and she controlled it on her chest before chipping it past an onrushing defender, setting herself up for a left-footed volley into the far corner to make it 5-1. Chelsea have started our Division 1 campaign with a strong win and sit second in the table, behind the leaders only on goal difference. The Blues now have a two-week break before returning to Women’s National League Cup action on Sunday 1 November. We travel to Oxford United Women in the first knockout round, facing a side who are top of the third tier and unbeaten. news.title: Rachael Adedini signs first professional contract with Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea can confirm that promising young forward Rachael Adedini has signed her first contract as a professional with the club. A dynamic and versatile forward, Adedini is a central striker, and can also play out wide. The 17-year-old has represented France Under-17s on 24 occasions and has played at Under-19 level twice. On putting pen to paper on her first professional deal, Adedini said: ‘I'm very happy to be here. I'm excited, and I'm grateful to be here. ‘I'm thankful to God, and the reason behind this is because my brother's a big fan, and we've always loved Chelsea, so playing here today is a massive pride for me and my family.’ The young forward was born in Le Havre in France. She has played at three consecutive Women’s Under-17 European Championships since the 2023/24 campaign and has stood out with nine goals in total. That strike rate has seen her equal Germany’s Shekiera Martinez as the all-time top scorer at the Women's Under-17 Euros. France made the final in 2026, narrowly losing to Germany with a 1-0 defeat. Adedini finished the tournament with the Golden Boot award after scoring in a 5-0 win over Poland and netting a brace in a 4-1 victory over Finland in the group stages. Everyone at Chelsea extends a warm welcome to Rachael, and we look forward to watching her progress.

news.title: George Weah recalls his ‘historic’ debut derby winner against Tottenham
news.body_en: All Chelsea eyes are looking ahead to Saturday’s derby with Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge. In the corresponding fixture just over a quarter-of-a-century ago, George Weah lit up a cold winter’s night by heading his name into Blues folklore with the winning goal on his debut. The megastar striker’s stay in west London wasn’t a long one, but he knew how to make an impression. There was a tangible sense of bristling excitement inside Stamford Bridge as Weah made his way to the touchline to prepare for his Chelsea debut early in the second half of a feisty league game against Tottenham in January 2000. The 1995 Ballon d’Or winner had only flown into London a few hours earlier, signing the relevant paperwork on a loan deal from AC Milan before making his way to the ground, where he was immediately named as a substitute by Blues boss Gianluca Vialli. Now, he was preparing to make his debut in the 56th minute of a floodlit London derby. The Liberian striker was one of the biggest names in world football at the time. He had been one of Milan’s star turns at a time when Serie A was the strongest league in Europe, and everyone had seen his famous goal against Verona in 1996, when he had picked up the ball inside his own box then proceeded to run the length of the pitch before guiding the ball into the far corner. However, the 33-year-old had fallen out of favour at the San Siro by the midway point of the 1999/2000 season and Chelsea – who had topped the UEFA Champions League group that Milan had propped up earlier that season – reacted quickest to the news that he might be available. Vialli wasted no time in putting him in the team, either, and when he emerged from the bench wearing Chelsea blue for the first time, Weah’s mere presence triggered an audible buzz, which broke into a monumental cheer as the world-famous striker entered the fray. Half-an-hour later, he was celebrating the winning goal – the only goal of the game – three minutes from time, in front of the Shed End. His powerful leap at the back post had taken him a full foot higher than Stephens Carr and Clemence, who floundered as Weah headed Dennis Wise’s cross past Ian Walker. His eyes wide with delight under the floodlights, Weah’s celebrations dominated the back pages the following morning. ‘Weah on the march with Luca’s army!’ read the headline on the inside back page of the Daily Mirror, punning on defeated Spurs’ famous FA Cup final song, while the looks of delight on the faces of his team-mates Jon Harley and Chris Sutton seemed to be derived almost as much from the presence of Weah in their midst as from the delirium of a late victory over our London rivals. He reflected on that moment a decade later in an interview for our official website. ‘My time with Chelsea was excellent – I came in for half a season and in the most important game, the first game, Chelsea won and I scored,’ recalled Weah. ‘It’s historical for me, it will forever remain in my mind and my heart, it was the day I came to Chelsea and I scored.’ Back-to-back draws in their previous two games had left Vialli with the feeling that he needed another option up front. The partnership of Tore Andre Flo and Gianfranco Zola was suffering a mid-season crisis of confidence, while big-money summer signing Sutton had failed to settle in. Weah’s arrival changed that, as Vialli decided to partner the Liberian with Sutton, viewing the physically imposing duo as an alternative double act to Zola and Flo. Sutton relished the chance to link up with the new arrival and teed up Weah for the second goal in our 2-1 win over Leicester City in the FA Cup fifth round. Up against a physical side, Vialli went for the lesser-spotted large and large partnership up top, and Sutton sent his man sprawling to the floor before pulling the ball back for Weah to sweep home across the goalkeeper. These days, Sutton’s rough stuff would almost certainly have been penalised by the officials, or their video assistants, but the goal stood and the Blues progressed past Martin O’Neill’s towering side after matching them for aggression and spirit. In the following round, against Gillingham at Stamford Bridge, Weah produced a moment of magic that drew gasps from the stands, casually leaning forward in the centre circle in anticipation of a dropping ball and flicking a volleyed pass over his head with his heel. The audacious pass found its mark and it was the highlight of a 5-0 win, in which Weah also registered his third goal for the club. In total, he struck five times in 15 games for the Blues and signed off with an FA Cup winner’s medal after starting in our 1-0 win over Aston Villa in the 2000 final. The striker bounced around the old Wembley pitch following the last-ever cup final under those famous twin towers wearing a vest with a specially printed message for his son. ‘I believe in God, Timothy,’ it read. ‘I won the last FA Cup at Wembley before it was destroyed and that was a big impact for me, it is history for me,’ the legendary striker said of that day. ‘The FA Cup is one of the best competitions in the world and is a huge part of the English culture. ‘It is what I used to watch on television and then I was part of it, so again I have to thank all of the people that made it possible: Vialli, Zola, Dennis Wise, Chris Sutton, all those guys who wanted me to be successful and made me comfortable.’ After retiring from club football in 2003, Weah became involved in politics and was elected President of Liberia in 2017. Timothy – the subject of his inspirational printed message at Wembley in 2000 – has gone on to become a professional footballer himself, playing internationally for the USA, where he was born and raised, at the FIFA World Cup in 2022 and 2026. He also made an appearance against Chelsea during the 2021/22 season, when he came on as substitute for Lille in the first leg of our Champions League last-16 tie. A generation later, many a Blues fan raised a smile as the sight of the name ‘Weah’ on the team-sheet brought back found memories of derby victory at the Bridge. - A version of this article first appeared in the matchday programme in 2022. news.title: OTD: Alex's Middlesbrough missile! 🚀
Analysis: How Chelsea's persistence paid off against Tottenham
news.body_en: Chelsea Women had never lost to Tottenham in any competition before Sunday's clash at Stamford Bridge. But that didn't mean it would be easy to record our 19th consecutive win against them. Despite what the 6-2 scoreline might suggest, it was far from straightforward. Their head coach Martin Ho had steered them into fourth position in the Women's Super League table before the match kicked off, and it was soon clear they were more resilient than before. Battling for every ball, Spurs kept around 50 per cent possession in the first half, and went in at the break with the scores even at 1-1. The Blues found another gear once the hour mark had passed and put the game out of sight, but an improved Tottenham had certainly made things difficult up to that point. Here's a look at how we secured the three points... Tottenham approached the match looking determined to break a run of 19 defeats against cross-city rivals Chelsea. A look at the stats showed they matched us in a number of areas, with seven shots on target to our eight, and 94 passes in the final third as opposed to our tally of 107. And while other teams sit in a low block against us, Spurs deserve credit for trying to secure a win at Stamford Bridge, even though they ultimately came up short of their objective. The momentum graph above indicates how they enjoyed sustained periods of pressure: in the opening minutes of the match, between the half-hour mark and half-time, and straight from the kick-off after the break. But when Sonia Bompastor made a triple change on the hour mark, Chelsea's strength in depth really shone through. Sjoeke Nusken and Maika Hamano scored our fourth and fifth goals of the afternoon not long after coming off the bench. We killed the game off in a matter of minutes, but the encounter was much more evenly matched until those aforementioned substitutions. Katie McCabe, like many others in the side, came into Sunday's match having represented her country during the international window. The Republic of Ireland captain helped them defeat Kazakhstan 12-0 on aggregate in a Women's World Cup qualifier, playing the 90 minutes and scoring in the 4-0 second-leg success in Cork last Tuesday. McCabe ranked highest of the Blues in terms of chances created (four) and crosses attempted (five). She also completed the second-highest number of passes (38) and ranked fifth in completed passes in the final third (seven). When the team scores six goals, performances like McCabe's can go under the radar, but she made a significant contribution to our success on Sunday. Playing just 68 minutes before being replaced by Nathalie Bjorn, Lucy Bronze put in another impressive performance in the heart of the defence on Sunday. Registering the assist for Lauren James' second strike of the afternoon, the Chelsea vice-captain made the most ball recoveries of any outfield player (eight), won the most tackles (five), and completed the most passes (40). Another player whose contribution may have been slightly overlooked in favour of the goalscorers at the Bridge on Sunday, but her touch map alone shows how much ground she covered, even though she was substituted with 20 minutes still to play. The Chelsea fans at Stamford Bridge were treated to another Lauren James show on Sunday, as she left them open-mouthed with her audacious strike from the byline in the first half. She then went for goal in a fashion that most other players would not consider, netting her second while leaning at an angle with a defender on her tail. Head coach Sonia Bompastor described her as a 'world-class player' in her post-match press conference, and it's not difficult to see why. Scoring a brace from only three shots on goal, her quality ensured we took the lead when the contest was extremely tight in the first half. Her two goals came from an xG (expected goals) rating of just 0.76, which shows just how difficult her chances were to convert. 'It's a big help when you have a player who can create from nothing,' said Bompastor afterwards. 'I want to also highlight the team performance. When individuals are performing, it's usually because the team is performing as well. The players around her are doing a job for her to express her quality on the ball.'

news.title: Analysis: Collective resilience and decisive Neto pivotal to Everton win
news.body_en: Saturday’s win at Everton included a first clean sheet in the Premier League since January, a star performance from Pedro Neto, and yet another goal scored early on in a half. Here we dissect some of the key elements behind a super success on Merseyside using statistics to come out of our maiden win at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. Xabi Alonso spoke in the build-up about the significance of matching Everton’s tenacious approach. It was something we managed to do for only 45 minutes at Brentford, and our manager said his team had learned from that disappointing second half at the Gtech Stadium in our last away game. Those learnings were clear to see as we went toe to toe with the Toffees physically. In what was a feisty first half, with five yellow cards shown before the 35th minute, we won six tackles to Everton’s four and came out on top in nine of the 10 aerial duels. By the final whistle, we had won more tackles, made more interceptions and fared better in the aerial and ground duels contested. We also ran further than Everton (114 kilometres to 111km) over the 115 minutes the contest ran to. Those successes helped us stymie Everton’s attack throughout. We limited our hosts to six shots, their fewest in a league game this season. Their total xG (expected goals) was 0.43, of which just 0.13 stemmed from open-play attempts. It was the first time since February they failed to score in a home game. While Everton completed more passes than us in the final third, our defensive fortitude and astute positioning ensured they were largely kept well away from our goal. We regularly forced them wide, from where we were able to deal with the 20 crosses they sent into our box. We thoroughly deserved a first league away clean sheet since last December and, as Alonso noted afterwards, it was the collective efforts of his side that earned it. Nobody epitomised that more than Pedro Neto. Of course, his first-ever Premier League brace stole the headlines and secured us the points, but the Portuguese showed his value defensively, too. He regained possession on five occasions – a figure only bettered by Morgan Rogers – and also won a joint-high three tackles. Alonso seemed surprised when a journalist described Neto as a wing-back after the match, with our manager preferring to label him as an attacker ‘who can do many things’. In the first half at Everton, Neto forced Jordan Pickford into a fingertip save with an effort from distance. After the break, he scored twice with precise left-footed shots, having manoeuvred himself into dangerous positions in the penalty box. Those three attempts amounted to just 0.37 xG, testament to the quality of his finishing. He also created a game-high five chances for his team-mates (his most since April 2025), and recorded a passing accuracy of 100 per cent in the final third – that despite only two Blues playing more passes in that area of the pitch. It has been a strong start to the season for Neto, with only eight players in the league having scored more goals than his three. He also ranks highly for take-ons, drives into the box and chances created. Allied to his defensive worth, it is obvious why Alonso is so happy to have him on our right flank. Neto’s first of the afternoon arrived just 43 seconds after the interval, continuing our remarkable record of scoring early in halves this season. We have now netted three times in the opening minute of a half (Joao Pedro vs Fulham and Bournemouth, Neto vs Everton) – already our joint-most in a Premier League season, along with 2011/12. We became the third team in Premier League history, and first since its inaugural season, to score in the opening minute of the second half in consecutive games. Eight of our 17 league goals this season have arrived in the opening four minutes of a half, and our nine scored in the first 10 minutes is the most any team has mustered in Premier League history after seven matches. It is certainly a useful habit to have – and if you’re coming to Saturday’s game against Tottenham, make sure you’re in your seat for the start of each half!

news.title: Ellie Carpenter on Chelsea's 'new era' after big win over Tottenham
news.body_en: Ellie Carpenter hailed a new-look Chelsea side after she scored a brace in a resounding 6-2 win over Tottenham at Stamford Bridge on Sunday. The Blues have netted 25 goals in our unbeaten start to the season, winning eight out of our ten matches. Carpenter has featured in all ten games and has three goals and three assists to her name. The right wing-back arrived from Lyon at the beginning of last season and can see the difference in the team’s performances this time around. ‘I would say it's like a new Chelsea,’ she said after Sunday's victory. ‘We're creating our own legacy, our own type of season this year. We're the 2026/27 Chelsea. ‘It's a new era, and this season we are really working collectively; everyone is together, and we’re taking things game by game. We don't want to look too far ahead of ourselves. We’ll just continue to try and put in the good performances.’ Chelsea had 20 players away on international duty across the world last week, returning only two days before we faced Tottenham in Women’s Super League action. Head coach Sonia Bompastor described the biggest challenge she faced during that period as ‘reconnecting quickly with the game model.' For that reason alone, Carpenter was proud of how the team responded to the challenge after a tough first half in which we went in all square at 1-1 at the interval. ‘It was a real team performance, especially after the international break,’ she explained. ‘Sometimes it can take a little bit to get going as a team. ‘But we had a lot of different goalscorers, and the impact off the bench was great. I was very happy to score. I have been working a lot in the final third this season, so I’m very happy to contribute to the win.’ Also netting a brace on Sunday was Lauren James, who scored from the tightest of angles and converted another difficult chance in the second half. Carpenter paid tribute to her talented team-mate and explained why she loves being on the same team as the Chelsea number ten. ‘Yeah, she's amazing,’ the Australian said. ‘Incredible footballer. I love watching her play when I'm on the pitch. She makes it look so easy; she's so talented, and I’m so happy she's a Blue.’

news.title: Forward voted as your Star of the Match against Tottenham!
news.body_en: Chelsea Women entertained the crowds at Stamford Bridge with a 6-2 victory over Tottenham on Sunday, and Blues fans have voted for their standout performer. The teams went in at the break with the scores locked at 1-1, as Lauren James' audacious opener from the dead-ball line was cancelled out by Matilda Vinberg's 41st-minute effort. But in the second half, the Blues went on a goalscoring spree as Ellie Carpenter put us back in front with an emphatic finish at the far post before James showed her skill once more with another sublime goal just after the hour mark. The second-half substitutes then weighed in, with Sjoeke Nusken smashing home our fourth, before a superb swerving long-range strike from Maika Hamano put us 5-1 in front. Carpenter then completed the rout with a fantastic turn and finish, sealing the 6-2 victory. news.title: Henderson: It is a privilege and honour to play in this team
news.body_en: Jordan Henderson has explained why the quality of team-mates around him means he is loving life at Chelsea after making his own mark on the pitch in our consecutive wins over Bournemouth and Everton. The midfielder’s introduction to the Chelsea supporters was delayed by an arm injury picked up with England at the FIFA World Cup in the summer, but he has been more than making up for lost time since his return to action. After marking his home debut with two goals and an assist – the first of those goals coming with just one minute on the clock – in the 5-1 win over Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge, he helped us to victory again as we defeated previously unbeaten Everton 2-0 on Saturday. 'I'm loving playing football at the minute,’ beamed Henderson after recording back-to-back wins with the Blues for the first time. ‘I’ve come back in the last month or so from my injury and it’s an absolute privilege and honour to be playing with some of the players in this team. 'I'm just enjoying it, working with them every day and playing with them out on the pitch. There's some top quality, top talent, here, and I really feel like the team's beginning to take shape in terms of the togetherness and everything. 'There's been a lot of new change in the summer – new coaching staff and players coming in – but I really feel that the togetherness is coming, not only in training during the week on the field, off the field as well. That's going to be important for us going forward and I'm loving every second of it.' Henderson won’t be resting on his laurels after those consecutive Premier League victories, though, as he knows there is still plenty more this Chelsea team is capable of if we continue developing under Xabi Alonso. ‘I know we've still got a lot to improve on as a team, but I feel as though in the last couple of weeks we're going in the right direction,’ he added. ‘So, we'll go back to the training ground and keep working hard for the next game.’ Now the focus turns to our next huge clash at Stamford Bridge! Henderson on a ‘vital’ three points and ‘controlled’ performance
news.body_en: Jordan Henderson was delighted to continue building momentum by recording back-to-back Premier League victories, with a first clean sheet in that competition to boot. Having brushed Bournemouth aside with an emphatic 5-1 victory at Stamford Bridge last week, Chelsea took that form on the road to inflict Everton’s first defeat of 2026/27, that 2-0 win also our first ever at their new Hill Dickinson Stadium home. With consecutive league wins in our pocket, which lifted us above the Toffees and into fourth in the Premier League standings, Henderson was left understandably satisfied with a job well done by the Blues on Merseyside on Saturday. ‘I thought it was a good performance and a good result in the end,’ said the midfielder. ‘Three points is always vital for us, especially away from home against a tough team who were unbeaten this season. ‘We knew it was going to be a difficult game, but I really liked the performance. I thought defensively we looked solid and we created some good chances to score two nice goals. Overall, I think it was a good day. ‘We wanted to back up last week by going there and putting on a good performance and getting the win, which we did.’ That sense of satisfaction is only enhanced by the feeling that Chelsea are finding the balance that Xabi Alonso had called for, by adding defensive steel to our free-scoring attack, with seven goals scored to one conceded across our last two matches after Saturday’s shut-out. ‘A clean sheet is always important and I know we haven't had enough of them for a while,’ he continued. ‘So to get one is nice, but I thought that overall our defending from start to finish was good. ‘I don't think we gave them too many chances at all, so that was really pleasing. We could have maybe scored one or two more goals, but overall I thought we controlled the game well and it's just about keep building and keep working.’ Henderson also had words of support for Emiliano Martinez, who was stretchered off the field against Everton and later underwent successful surgery on a fractured jaw, wishing our goalkeeper a speedy recovery. ‘All the lads and everyone will be thinking of him, of course, and texting him. So fingers crossed he can be back with us pretty soon because he's a really important figure, not only on the pitch but around the dressing room.’ Now the focus turns to our next huge clash at Stamford Bridge! news.title: Erin reacts post-Spurs 🤩
Cuthbert on her return and 'ruthless' Bompastor
news.body_en: Chelsea captain Erin Cuthbert was delighted to make her return from injury during our 6-2 win over Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on Sunday afternoon. The skipper, who has been working her way back to fitness after a knee problem sustained while on international duty in June, was given a rousing reception by the Blues supporters when she was introduced after an hour on Sunday. Cuthbert took over the armband from previous captain Millie Bright back in August, but had to wait until our 10th match of the campaign to make her first appearance since the news was announced. Call it good fortune or merely a coincidence, but Lauren James scored our third goal only a minute after her introduction, with Sjoeke Nusken following up with our fourth shortly afterwards. 'It was a bit mental, a bit chaotic!' said Cuthbert afterwards. 'I came on, and we scored quite early, so that kind of settled the nerves a little bit. 'It's always tough to come in during a high-pressure game, but I loved every minute of being back on the pitch, and back at Stamford Bridge. When we're playing like that, it's a fun place.' It has been four-and-a-half months of intense rehab work for Cuthbert to regain match fitness and now she is back she understands that she will have to earn her place in the team. 'Honestly, I felt so ready,' the midfielder continued. 'I had a few set-backs here and there during the recovery. I was targeting the start of the season, and it's five weeks in now, so that's how it went for me. 'I've been working hard in the background. It can be hard to be out when the team are doing really well, and although it's great to watch, I just want to be out there helping the team. 'We've got a single game week this week, and no one is going to know what to do with themselves. The competition is going to be high in training. We will have to perform if we want a place in the starting line-up, and that's what you want as a player. 'That's why I've been at a club like Chelsea for so long because I enjoy the competition. We've got so many really good players in the midfield and across the pitch competing in other positions, and I really thrive under pressure. 'Today it was about me coming on and trying to make an impact, and I got booked, so that's one way to make an impact!' Cuthbert went on to detail exactly how head coach Sonia Bompastor drives the standards among the team, and how hard the players have to work to meet her expectations. 'I don't envy the manager's decision because she's got 25 international players to manage, and that's her job,' the captain explained. 'As players, we've got to make her job as hard as we possibly can, and over the course of the season, we are going to need everybody. 'We've got some real tough spells coming up. I think we've got another eight games in this block before the next international break so everybody will get their moment and it's about being ready to take it when it comes. 'Sonia demands standards in training every single day. She pushes you. She wants the best from her team, and she's ruthless. She wants a high press every single second. And if she doesn't get it from the people on the pitch, she'll get it from the people sitting on the side.'

news.title: 'It was important for us to connect to the game'
Bompastor gives Girma update and praises 'unbelievable' Chelsea fans
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor was delighted with her side after Chelsea Women's 6-2 win over Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on Sunday afternoon and singled out the impact of the supporters on the team's performance. A brace each from Ellie Carpenter and Lauren James, plus goals from substitutes Maika Hamano and Sjoeke Nusken, contributed to the 6-2 victory on Bompastor's 50th game in the Women's Super League. The result means we continue our unbeaten start to the campaign, with five wins and one draw from our opening six league matches this season. 'I'm pleased with the performance and the result,' said the head coach afterwards. 'I was convinced coming into this game, we would need players who would come in and bring a big impact and fresh legs. 'On the back of the international break, we can talk about the tactical aspects, but it was probably the most important thing to have players who impacted the game the way they did today. So it's good when you have depth in the squad, a lot of players available, and the quality of the players who are coming in.' The fans at Stamford Bridge were treated to a big win for Chelsea on Sunday afternoon, with eight goals scored in total. We are now playing all of our WSL matches at Stamford Bridge and the crowd noise has been excellent throughout. That sentiment was echoed by our head coach. 'The atmosphere today was great in the stadium,' continued Bompastor. 'The fans were unbelievable. It helps when they can see many goals. Both teams need to play well for them to see the quality of football on the pitch. So credit to Chelsea, but also to Tottenham for that. 'I feel like they really enjoyed it, especially with the win at the end and the three points.' Naomi Girma was missing from the squad against Spurs, and Bompastor gave an update on her condition. 'Naomi picked up a small injury in her calf before the international break,' she explained. 'That's why she's out of the squad. But right now I have depth in the squad. I have a lot of high-quality competition.' Praising the contribution of James after her two superb goals this afternoon, Bompastor said: 'When LJ is playing at this level, we are talking about a top-class player, a world-class player. She creates things for herself by herself with the quality she has on the ball. 'It's a big help when you have a player who can create from nothing. I want to also highlight the team performance. When individuals are performing, it's usually because the team is performing as well. The players around her are doing a job for her to express her quality on the ball.' James came into Sunday's clash on the back of a brace for England during Tuesday evening's 5-0 win over Greece. Bompastor explained that her international performances helped fuel today's outstanding display. 'It was a bit more difficult for her before the international break,' said the head coach. 'Going with England was a big boost and I think she played really well, and we are now getting the benefit of that, so it's good.'

news.title: Match report: Chelsea Women 6-2 Tottenham
news.body_en: A brilliant second-half performance saw Chelsea Women defeat Tottenham Hotspur 6-2 at Stamford Bridge, with a brace each from Ellie Carpenter and Lauren James. Tottenham came into the encounter in good form, aside from a heavy defeat to London City Lionesses before the international break. And early on, they showed exactly why they had risen to fourth in the table as they played with determination from the get-go. Yet it was Chelsea who took the lead thanks to a brilliant solo effort from Lauren James, as she used her skill to drive to the byline and fire a perfect shot over the line from what first looked to be an impossible angle. Away sides often let their heads drop when the Blues take the lead at home, but Spurs stuck to their plan, kept pushing forward and got their reward when Matilda Vinberg headed in from close range. The second half was a different story. A fine finish from Ellie Carpenter put the Blues back in front before another outstanding solo effort from James gave us breathing room with an hour gone. Substitute Sjoeke Nusken smashed in emphatically following some excellent wing play from Alyssa Thompson, before Maika Hamano netted against her former club with a stunning strike from range. Tottenham pulled back a consolation goal with three minutes of normal time remaining, before Carpenter completed her brace with composure in stoppage time. It was a positive day all around for the Blues, as the big win coincided with the first minutes this season for new club captain Erin Cuthbert as she came on after an hour. This Chelsea side seems to be looking more impressive every week. Bompastor made four alterations to her line-up, exchanging Sandy Baltimore, Veerle Buurman, Hamano and Nusken for James, Katie McCabe, Lexi Potter and Thompson. It was Spurs who started on the front foot in the opening minutes, and Hannah Hampton had to be alert and make a save when the space suddenly opened up for Signe Gaupset in a central position. But then the Blues had a chance of our own as Carpenter drove to the byline and put a dangerous ball in across the byline. Striker Melvine Malard received the cross no more than a yard out, but with her back to goal just couldn't steer the ball across the line. Spurs had come to Stamford Bridge ready to fight for every ball. After 15 minutes, there was not much between the sides and the possession counter read at 50 per cent each. With a determined Spurs making things difficult, it took a magnificent solo effort from James to unlock their defence. Stealing the ball from Toko Koga on the left flank, our No10 drove towards the dead-ball line. Most players would've run out of space at the by-line, but not James. Instead, she unleashed a shot with sublime skill and pure power, beating the goalkeeper as the ball crossed the line in the opposite corner. Yet Spurs were undeterred. Kadeisha Buchanan made a key intervention from a Vinberg cross, preventing the ball from reaching the onrushing Cathinka Tandberg as they continued to press forward towards goal. Koga had recovered her composure from losing the ball to James as she made a key block on Carpenter up the other end. Tottenham's persistence paid off shortly before half-time. Arriving late into the final third, Julie Blakstad picked up the ball just outside the penalty area, swinging a cross into the far post. Vinberg rose highest, nodding home from close range to put the visitors level. Spurs came out brightly once again in the second half, but the best chance in the early stages of the second half fell to Chelsea. Lexi Potter's determination in midfield and pass to Malard created an opening for the striker, but her curling effort from the corner of the penalty area went over the bar. Just when the outcome of the contest looked uncertain, Thompson used her pace to breeze past her marker, skipping over a challenge on the edge of the box before squaring the ball to Carpenter. The Australian made no mistake with her powerful finish high into the back of the net, putting the Blues back in front in style. Bompastor then made a triple change. Among the substitutes was Cuthbert, making her first appearance for Chelsea this season, and our new captain received a rousing reception from the Blues supporters in the stands at Stamford Bridge. Cuthbert had been on the pitch for less than a couple of minutes when James took matters into her own hands again. Breaking free of the backpedalling defenders, she burst into the box and used her low centre of gravity to lean backwards and curl another superb shot into the bottom corner. After what had been a truly difficult contest, Chelsea then found yet another gear. Keira Walsh chipped a delicate pass to substitute Nusken, who had found space in the box, and the midfielder lashed in a powerful strike to put us 4-1 in front. The Germany international then almost handed James her hat-trick, but grateful goalkeeper Lize Kop was able to dive on the ball and just about prevent her shot from crossing the line. Spurs proved dangerous in attack once again when Hampton made an excellent save from a Kirsty Hanson shot, and showed the quickest reactions when she collected the follow-up. Facing her former club for the first time since last season's loan spell, Hamano said before the match that her dream is to one day win the prestigious Ballon d'Or trophy. Her 86th-minute strike was certainly worthy of a player of that calibre, netting with a magnificent swerving effort from almost 30 yards out. Those inside the stadium were still recovering from Hamano's brilliant effort when Spurs grabbed a consolation through Gaupset, but there was still more to come from the Blues. The emphatic London derby win was sealed when Walsh picked out Carpenter in the box, and the wing-back then completed her brace with a wonderful turn and finish. A brilliantly entertaining afternoon for the Chelsea faithful at the Bridge. We go top of the WSL table, pending Manchester City's result. We face newly-promoted Crystal Palace in Women's Super League action over at the Borough Sports Ground in Sutton. news.title: Hato on Cobham work paying off with ‘solid’ clean sheet
news.body_en: Jorrel Hato was pleased to see the hard work put in on the training pitch in recent weeks come to fruition with an important win at Everton, which he believes provides a strong platform to continue building on. A brace of goals by Pedro Neto at either end of the second half secured our first-ever three points at the Hill Dickinson Stadium and moved us up to fourth place in the Premier League table with a 2-0 victory over the Toffees. However, just as important as the winning goals was the clean sheet at the other end of the pitch, our first in the league of 2026/27 under Xabi Alonso. Speaking after the win, Hato confirmed that shut-out was a key aim for the Blues going into this game and something they had been working hard to achieve on the training pitch at Cobham recently. ‘That was one of our goals,’ said the defender. ‘Of course, we score a lot of goals, everyone knows this, but now we finally have our own clean sheet and as a team it's good. ‘We didn't give many chances away, or big chances, so that's solid and we keep going. Now we have to go forward with it and keep as many clean sheets as we can. ‘When we came back from the international break, everyone knew that we have a good team and we score a lot of goals, but defensively it had to be better. We had to do it, and I think we showed it against Bournemouth and again against Everton.’ That clean sheet arrived despite the loss of Emiliano Martinez during the second half to a nasty injury, with it being confirmed this morning that our goalkeeper has now undergone successful surgery on a fractured jaw. ‘Of course, when a moment like this happens, everyone is in shock. But of course, the game goes on for another 20 minutes. So we were just saying to each other: “stay focused”. I think we did a good job. We scored to make it 2-0 and finish off the game.’ Despite the set-back of losing Martinez, it was a strong second-half showing from the Blues on Merseyside to claim all the points and leapfrog opponents Everton in the standings. Now, Hato is looking to keep building on the momentum from that victory and the previous week’s win over Bournemouth, with a London derby against Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge to come next. ‘I think we started well after the break, and now it’s two games and two wins, so we have to keep going,’ the Dutchman added. ‘There are a lot of games coming, and great games to play as well, so we have to keep going.’ Now the focus turns to our next huge clash at Stamford Bridge! news.title: Injury update: Emiliano Martinez
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club has released the following update on Emiliano Martinez. Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez has undergone successful surgery on a fractured jaw. Martinez was injured following a collision midway through the second half of our 2-0 victory over Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday. Martinez was taken to hospital for further assessment, which confirmed a fractured jaw that required surgery. Everyone at Chelsea wishes Emi a speedy recovery and will support him throughout.

news.title: Alonso outlines Neto’s ‘great qualities’ and why Blues trio pleased him so much
news.body_en: In what was, for long periods, a tight game at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, Pedro Neto’s two well-taken goals made the difference. For Xabi Alonso, it was yet another example of what the Portuguese offers this Chelsea team. With his pair of clinical left-footed finishes against Everton, Neto took his tally for the season to four goals. That figure is already almost half of the ten he notched in 2025/26. There is plenty more to Neto’s game than goals, though. Alonso has deployed him in a right-sided position so far this season. It is a role which allows him to showcase his attacking intent while continually contributing defensively, utilising his work rate and positional discipline. Click to shop the third kit now ‘You can call him whatever – winger, wing-back, attacker, defender – because he can do many things,’ said Alonso. ‘Pedro has great qualities. He’s always a threat, has a great competitive level, he can run, do one-v-ones, can score goals. ‘He’s so competitive. When he’s close to the action, he’s a threat against any full-back. When he’s on the last line or in between, he connects well with the players around, with Joao (Pedro), with Cole (Palmer), with Josh (Acheampong) as well. They worked really well, and I’m happy he could score.’ So far this season it has been the names of Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers that have stolen the headlines. While that trio did not score or assist on Saturday, Alonso was still delighted with their contributions. They led from the front and set the tone for a fantastic collective showing. ‘For me they played a fantastic game,’ he said. ‘They worked really hard. They were helping the team, Morgan on the wing, Cole and Joao in the middle. We need that to win as a team, so many positives from the game.’ Three points secured - now, the focus turns to our next huge clash at Stamford Bridge! news.title: Pedro Neto explains how Chelsea are implementing new Xabi Alonso ideas
news.body_en: It’s now two impressive wins over two challenging Premier League opponents for Chelsea since the international break. And Blues winger Pedro Neto says that it is not by chance. The opening weeks of our campaign were entertaining, if not entirely convincing. Our attacking play was undeniably exciting and we scored plenty of goals, but Alonso's side were also conceding an average of two a game in the top flight. Alonso accepted that wasn't sustainable and emphasised the need for improvement ahead of the three-week international break, which gave him and the Chelsea coaching staff quality time to work with the players not away representing their countries. That practice was put into action against Bournemouth last weekend. The attacking adventure and invention remained, but the Blues were far more solid defensively, something aided by Moises Caicedo returning from injury and Jordan Henderson making his home debut. There was greater solidity to our display at Everton, with the Toffees, aside from two good first-half opportunities, restricted across the 90 minutes. It was notable that after establishing a lead through Pedro Neto's well-taken finish, the home side couldn't build momentum and genuinely threaten our goal. They ended with an expected goals total of 0.43. Neto credited a half-time tweak from Alonso to improve our build-up as an important factor in the victory, but also explained that the work done during the international break has been implemented in our past two matches. He said: 'I think during the international break, the manager had a little bit more time to focus on different ideas and try new things, and since we came back, he has been really vocal about that. 'We follow his ideas and we put effort into them, which is most important. And as you saw [against Everton] we had a really good game.' 'The ambition [for the rest of the season] is to take things game by game and then we will see what will happen. The important thing is that we approach every game like it’s the last one and that we continue to compete.'

news.title: Full Match: Everton vs Chelsea
Extended: Everton 0-2 Chelsea
Pedro Neto on the mentality and half-time tweak that downed Everton
news.body_en: Pedro Neto says the mentality of Chelsea's players to 'fight and win duels' against Everton, coupled with half-time tactical tweaks by manager Xabi Alonso, was crucial to the Blues recording a 2-0 win at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. A trip to the blue half of Merseyside is rarely easy. At Goodison Park, Everton supporters would create a hostile atmosphere that could suffocate visiting sides. The same can happen at their new stadium, as the Blues found out first-hand last term. It's why Alonso highlighted the importance of having the right mentality ahead of the game. The Chelsea manager's words were heeded. In a feisty opening 45 minutes, we stood up to the physical challenge posed by the Toffees. Strong challenges were not shirked. Loose balls were hotly contested. It gave the Blues a platform to build on, and in the second half, after Alonso altered how Chelsea built possession, we took control. Click to shop the third kit now Neto netted just 43 seconds after the restart, beating Jordan Pickford with a well-placed finish. We muted Everton's potential response, although at a cost as Emi Martinez was stretchered off after a heavy collision with Jarrad Branthwaite. The Blues handled the injury professionally, and in the 90th minute, Neto reacted quickest to a blocked Jordan Henderson free-kick and swept the ball home to seal our victory. 'Really hard three points playing away at this difficult stadium,' the Portugal international reflected after celebrating with the travelling Chelsea supporters. 'A word to our team-mate, who unfortunately got an injury, but we are really happy to get a win at this difficult stadium. 'They are a team that is very physical and have worked with the coach (David Moyes) for nearly two years – and he has really good ideas. They fight, they win duels and are really tough. But we came here with the same mentality and knew we had to run more than them and fight more than them.' Scoring early in halves has become a recurring theme of the Blues season, and Neto's opener was the latest example of Alonso's side catching another team off guard. Neto highlighted that, at the interval, the Chelsea manager and staff tweaked how the Blues would use the ball after spotting Everton pressing man-to-man in the opening period. It quickly paid off. 'We adjusted a little bit because we were seeing that they were pressing man-to-man on the goal kicks,' he explained. 'We won some duels in the first phase and got to the goal with an unbelievable play from Jorrel (Hato), then I got the ball to my feet and tried to finish. I’m happy I could do it.' Martinez's injury was the only disappointing note of the afternoon. Alonso confirmed after the game that the Argentinian was conscious when he left the stadium and was undergoing precautionary tests at a local hospital. The Blues goalkeeper certainly contributed to our victory with important saves in the first half. His replacement, Mike Penders, also kept Everton at bay as we recorded our first Premier League clean sheet of the campaign. Neto dedicated the shutout, and the victory, to Martinez. ‘This win is for him; he deserves it as he did a really good job. We hope he is okay and we are really happy to get the win for him. 'It’s a deserved clean sheet, and we've been waiting for a long time. He deserves it as well. He’s a great guy and I hope we continue like this to give him more.'

news.title: Xabi Alonso reflects on a ‘serious, solid, very good’ away win
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso was delighted with the way his Chelsea team acquitted themselves at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, with a blend of defensive discipline, attacking cohesion and clinical finishing from Pedro Neto earning us three points and a first league clean sheet since January. Neto bagged a second-half brace to secure us a 2-0 victory against Everton, and the Blues matched Everton’s intensity, particularly in a tetchy opening 45 minutes when tempers flared. We took control of the contest right after the restart, though, and saw out the result with relative comfort, even adding a second late on to ensure there was no late drama during the 11 minutes added on following an injury to Emiliano Martinez. It was no surprise, then, that Alonso was so pleased afterwards. Click to shop the third kit now ‘We are very happy with the result and the performance,’ he said. ‘We needed one of these wins away, where we have played very professionally and seriously, looking solid. It was a very good win. We got many things right. ‘We looked in control of the game, there were moments for sure when we had to defend, especially in the first half, but overall the team looked mature, knew what to do in each moment, and knew we’d have our own moment. That happened in the second half. ‘After that, we were good with the ball, creating chances and not conceding much. To win away is always tough, and we got the clean sheet. We knew it was a matter of time and finally we got it.’ That clean sheet has been elusive, but it was thoroughly well earned. Martinez and his replacement Mike Penders stood tall when required, but in truth we restricted Everton to very few clear opportunities. And Alonso wants to use this shutout as a platform to build upon. ‘We need to keep working; it’s just one game,’ he pointed out. ‘One [clean sheet this season] would be very poor; we need to get many more clean sheets in the rest of the league games. 'The first of the season feels good, so we have to keep going in this way, working well and being serious, and knowing that wherever we go we can play in an efficient and professional way, as we did today.’ Three points secured - now, the focus turns to our next huge clash at Stamford Bridge! news.title: Match report: Everton 0-2 Chelsea
news.body_en: Pedro Neto goals right at the start and end of the second half secured Chelsea a superb first win against Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. The Blues battled hard in a fractious opening 45 minutes, matching Everton’s intensity and energy, just as Xabi Alonso had demanded pre-match. We might have opened the scoring through Moises Caicedo or Maxence Lacroix before Neto broke the deadlock just 43 seconds after the restart, tucking his finish away after fine work from Jorrel Hato down the left. The only disappointment on the day was what looked a nasty injury suffered by Emiliano Martinez, who was replaced by Mike Penders with plenty of the game remaining. We continued to stand tall in defence, though, and sealed the win when Neto swept home a loose ball from 12 yards out. As satisfying as three well-earned points on the road is a first clean sheet in the Premier League since January, no mean feat in a fixture in which shutouts and indeed wins have been hard to come by in recent years. Alonso made a solitary change to the side that defeated Bournemouth, with Hato coming in for Pep Chavarria on the left-hand side of defence after the Spaniard picked up a knock in training yesterday. There was to be no early goal for Chelsea as both sides scrapped hard in the opening stages. Much of the play was restricted to action in the middle third of the pitch. The first shot in anger arrived on 15 minutes from the left foot of Cole Palmer, 20 yards out, with Jordan Pickford equal to it. A sustained spell of Chelsea possession and territorial dominance culminated in our best chance yet after Neto got in down the right and cut the ball back to Jordan Henderson, whose shot was blocked before it could test Pickford. Martinez made his first save to deny Merlin Rohl but was then penalised for holding onto the ball too long. From the resulting corner, a second cross from Jack Grealish found an unmarked Thierno Barry, who headed straight at Martinez. With the half-hour mark approaching, Martinez was at full stretch to tip Grealish’s bouncing volley over. The ill-feeling continued. A coming-together inside our half resulted in cards shown to James Tarkowski and Morgan Rogers, taking the number of players booked up to five with just 34 minutes played. Our first corner of the game, with half-time approaching, almost yielded a spectacular opening goal. Henderson’s deep corner picked out Caicedo running round the back, and he couldn’t have met his volley any sweeter, displaying exemplary technique. Unfortunately, it rattled the crossbar rather than nestling in the net as the strike deserved. Before the half-time whistle brought an end to a hard-fought 45 minutes of football, Pickford made one more save, tipping Neto’s long-range shot over. From the flurry of Blues corners that followed, Lacroix saw his goalbound header hacked off the line by Harrison Armstrong. We may not have scored early in the first half, but we did in the second! A cute backheel from Rogers released the bombarding Hato, who strode beyond Ainsley Maitland-Niles. His centre missed Palmer but reached Neto, unmarked. He set himself and swept his finish under the outstretched arm of Pickford. Just 43 seconds had elapsed since the restart. We have now scored three goals in the opening minute of a half in the Premier League this season, already our joint-most in a single campaign, alongside 2011/12. Rogers had a shot well blocked by Rohl as we sought a quick second, and an impudent long-range chip from Palmer had Pickford worried but drifted over his crossbar. Midway through the second half, Martinez bravely cleared an inswinging free-kick and collided with Jarrad Branthwaite and Thierno Barry in the process. After lengthy treatment totalling ten minutes, our keeper was replaced by Penders, making his Premier League debut. The Belgian’s first contribution of note was a superb punch from just inside his box to clear a cross. We continued to defend resolutely, and almost hit the Toffees on the break with a second. Palmer had options left and right and opted to play in Joao Pedro, but Pickford stood tall to save. However, we did make the game safe just before the clock ticked over to 90. Henderson’s attempt at replicating his free-kick heroics from last weekend fell short, with the wall blocking his shot, but the loose ball fell kindly to Neto. He intelligently delayed shooting until the space was there to do so, and then rolled his strike into the opposite corner from where he had tucked away his first. The Chelsea supporters had been enjoying themselves throughout the second half in the Merseyside sunshine, and now they had extra cause for celebration as we negotiated 11 added minutes to earn a fine away victory. The Blues rise above Everton in the formative table ahead of the rest of this weekend's Premier League action. A big London derby at the Bridge is up next, with Tottenham visiting next Saturday 24 October for a 5.30pm kick-off.
